results.content: | Late, but for anyone landing here from search, the numbers in your error work out exactly.  Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M has 48 layers, 8 KV heads and head\_dim 128, so the KV cache is 2 × 48 × 8 × 128 × 2 bytes = 192 KiB per token in BF16.    Your log's 73,792 tokens × 192 KiB = 13.5 GiB. That's what was left for cache: 0.9 × 47.5 GiB usable on the A6000 = 42.8 GiB, minus ~27.5 GiB of BF16 weights (14.7B params × 2 bytes), minus ~1.7 GiB for the profiling pass, CUDA graphs and non-torch memory. [...] non-torch memory.  The full 1,010,000 tokens would need about 185 GiB of cache for a single request (~92 GiB with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`). That's multi-GPU no matter what.   On one A6000, `--max-model-len 65536` (12 GiB of cache) works as is, or add `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` to get ~147K tokens out of the same 13.5 GiB.  I built a free vLLM calculator that does this for a given model, GPU and flags (you can load this model by its HF id). It's checked against posted vLLM startup logs:  | [...] you are running in `auto` mode which defaults to FP16, each of those 14 billion parameters takes up 2 bytes of memory. That means the model weights alone are occupying about 28 or 29 GB of your VRAM. Since vLLM reserves a specific percentage of the GPU for overhead and execution, you are likely left with only about 14 GB of free space for the KV cache.
